question: Should I quit my job to build my own thing?

cells.text: Quit immediately to honor the divine spark within you. Your soul's growth is stunted by corporate drudgery, and your primary duty is to follow your unique spiritual calling wherever it leads.
You must leave your job if it no longer resonates with your inner truth. Building your own thing allows you to align your energy with the universe and manifest a reality that truly feeds your spirit.
Only quit if your new venture is a spiritual gift to those around you. Your personal liberation is meaningful only when it creates a sanctuary where others can also find their higher purpose.
Abandon your private ambitions and quit only to serve the collective divine will. Your work must become a selfless sacrifice dedicated to the spiritual elevation of all humanity.
Quit now because you owe it to yourself to see what you are truly capable of. Building your own thing is the ultimate expression of self-actualization and the only way to achieve personal greatness.
Take the leap so you can express the unique vision that only you possess. You find your best self when you are creating something original that also inspires and uplifts your peers.
You should quit if your project addresses the spiritual and emotional needs of the community. Success is measured by how much compassion and connection your new venture brings into the world.
Leave your job only to build a new model of living that fosters harmony for everyone. Your individual initiative must serve as a blueprint for a more enlightened and unified society.

Quit only if you have a proven product and enough runway to ensure your personal financial independence. Logic dictates that you must secure your own material survival before chasing any creative whims.
Make the move if the data suggests your skills will fetch a higher price on the open market. Balancing your personal goals with current economic demand is the only sustainable way to succeed.
Pursue your own thing if it solves a practical problem for the common good. Individual effort is most effective when it builds tangible tools that make life better for the people in your city.

You should stay where you are unless quitting allows you to build a more efficient system for the public. Your individual desires are secondary to the smooth functioning of the services society relies on.
Quit the moment your own business generates a higher return on investment than your salary. Your time is a commodity, and you should always sell it to the highest bidder—which is usually yourself.

Leave your job to seize a market share that your current employer is too slow to capture. Victory belongs to the individual who can most aggressively outmaneuver the competition and accumulate assets.

You should only quit if you plan to build a worker-owned entity that shares its wealth. Individual ventures are fragile, but a collective material foundation ensures security and prosperity for all members.

Do not quit to become another boss; instead, stay and organize your workplace for the benefit of all workers. True material progress comes from collective action against the ownership class, not from starting a private business.
